entities.summary:
Polygnotus of Thasos was a renowned ancient Greek painter active in the mid-5th century BC, considered by later scholars to be one of the first great painters, sometimes even credited with inventing the artform.

He was born in Thasos, a Greek island in the Aegean Sea, and died in Athens, Greece, in 500 BCE. Polygnotus's significance lies in his contributions to the development of Western art, particularly in the fields of painting and fresco.

His most famous work, the 'Alexander' frieze, is now lost, but his influence can be seen in the works of later Greek painters, such as Apelles and Callicrates. Polygnotus's innovative techniques and artistic style helped shape the aesthetic of ancient Greek art, which in turn influenced the development of Western art for centuries to come.

The legacy of Polygnotus of Thasos can be seen in the many museums and galleries around the world that showcase his works or those of his contemporaries. Today, he is remembered as a pioneering artist who played a crucial role in shaping the course of Western art history.

Polygnotus of Thasos was a key figure in the cultural and artistic landscape of ancient Greece, and his impact can still be felt in the art world today.
